title: Shadows, Spacing, Quick Add and Tap Signals

items.title: Remove the Bottom-Right Drop Shadow
items.why: Every card has a hard black shadow 4 px to the bottom-right. To fit that shadow, each card is also nudged 2 px to the left. That nudge is why the Coach's Pick card was cut off on the left of the screen in your screenshot. Removing the shadow fixes the cut-off too. Black borders stay either way.

options.label: Cards flat, buttons keep a small shadow
options.desc: Cards and tiles lose the shadow. Buttons (Enter the Chamber, Today, Close) keep a small one, so they still look pressable.

options.label: Everything flat
options.desc: No offset shadow anywhere: cards, buttons, chips, the + button and the Quick Add menu.

items.area: Whole app · bottom of every tab
items.title: Keep Content Clear of the Bottom Bar
items.why:
Found the cause. Goku measures the bar to know how much empty space to leave at the bottom of each page, but it measures only the bar's inside. That leaves out its padding, its border and the iPhone's home-bar area (about 34 px). The round + button also pokes 22 px above the bar. Together that hides roughly 50 to 80 px of the page.

The fix measures the whole bar plus the + button. The same fix leaves a gap above the fixed buttons at the bottom of sheets. That's where step 2 of the Pike push-up ran under “Edit loads and drop chain” in your screenshot.

now.caption: Your screenshot: Add exercise under the bar
Your screenshot: step 2 under the button

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: The last thing on every page stops above the bar and the + button.

items.title: Quick Add Menu Without Overlaps
items.why: Today it fans out 6 buttons on one small half circle, so they overlap. Both choices use your two groups: Food & Drink (Food, Water, Supplements) and Activity (Train, Add Exercise, Log Activity, Rest Day). Supplements is new here; today it's only on the Nutrition tab. The same two groups can be used anywhere else that lists these.

options.label: Two big group buttons, then their items
options.desc: Tap + and you see Food & Drink and Activity. Tapping one fans out only its 3 or 4 items, with room between them. It takes one more tap than today.

options.label: One panel with both groups
options.desc: Tap + and a panel slides up with both groups as labeled rows of buttons. Every item is still one tap away, and nothing can overlap.

items.title: What You See After Tapping Activity (Option A)
items.why: Only matters if you picked “Two big group buttons” above. This is the second step: Activity's four items, spaced so they don't touch.

items.title: Title Case for Headings and Labels
items.why:
“Quick add” becomes “Quick Add”, “Interaction check” becomes “Interaction Check”, “Supplements to check” becomes “Supplements to Check”, and “Protein and nutrients” becomes “Protein & Nutrients”. Small words (a, and, of, to, the, for) stay lowercase unless they come first. Units (g, oz, cal), brand names and anything you type stay exactly as they are.

Also shortened, as you asked: “Fuel timing for when you train” becomes “Fuel Timing”.

options.label: Headings, labels, buttons, tabs and exercise names
options.desc: e.g. “Quick Add”, “Last Session”, “Enter the Chamber”, “Start Workout”, “Edit Loads and Drop Chain”, “Pike Push-Up”.

options.label: Same, but exercise and food names stay as they are
options.desc: “Pike push-up” and “Bodyweight squat” stay sentence case. Everything else is Title Case.

options.label: Headings and labels only
options.desc: Buttons stay sentence case: “Enter the chamber”, “Start workout”.

items.title: The Orange Edge on Text Boxes
items.why:
Your question C: the orange edge isn't a style for that one box. It marks the box the cursor is in. The Interaction Check puts the cursor in “Your Medicines” when it opens, so only that box has it.

It's drawn 2 px outside the box. That's why it was cut off at both sides of the screen (B) and ran into the Add button (A). Both choices also add a proper gap between the box and the Add button.

Related: the orange ring that appears inside the Close button whenever a sheet opens (your Pike push-up and ki screenshots) is the same marker. It would only show when using a keyboard.

options.label: Orange edge inside the box you're typing in
options.desc: Same rule for every box in the app. It never pokes past the screen or into the next button.

options.label: No colored edge at all
options.desc: Only the blinking cursor shows where you're typing.

items.title: Ki and Gravity
items.why:
What they actually do: the 4 gravity levels set the workout. ×10 is 3 rounds with 90 s rest. ×20 is 4 rounds with 75 s rest. ×50 is 4 rounds with 45 s rest. ×100 is 5 rounds with 30 s rest. The higher levels also take sets to failure with drops. The ki question only suggests a level from how you feel. So the function is real; the names hide it.

With A or B, Home also uses plain words: “Gravity chamber · today” becomes “Today's Workout”, “×50 gravity” becomes “Hard”, and “Today's ki” becomes “Today's Progress”. The Dragon Ball look and the themes stay.

The “Plain” look in Settings already uses plain words, but it also drops the Dragon Ball style everywhere else.

options.label: Plain levels, no ki question
options.desc: Train opens Today's Workout: Easy, Medium, Hard or Max, with the rounds and rest spelled out, then Start Workout. One less screen.

options.label: Plain levels, keep a short “How do you feel?”
options.desc: Same plain levels. A 4-choice feeling question still suggests one.

items.area: Whole app · what can be tapped
items.title: Make Tappable Things Obvious
items.why:
Today tap signals are mixed: some rows end in ›, some links are underlined, some folds have nothing at all. On iPhone the fold arrow on Fuel Timing, How You Feel and the Library groups doesn't show, because of how those headers are styled. That's why Fuel Timing looked exactly like Last Session and Food Today.

The example cards are from the Stats view.

now.caption: Your screenshot: only Fuel timing can be tapped

options.label: An orange › or “Show ▾” on everything tappable
options.desc: Cards that open something end in ›. Cards that unfold end in Show ▾. Cards with neither only show information.

options.label: Orange border and light fill on everything tappable
options.desc: Information cards keep the black border.

items.title: Show Nutrients Without a Tap
items.why: Today the panel shows only calories until you tap the small “Protein and nutrients” link. Apps like Cronometer and MacroFactor keep protein, carbs and fat on the main log screen for this reason.

options.label: Protein bar and 4 tiles always showing
options.desc: The % split, your protein range and the full nutrient list are behind one clear “All Nutrients ›” link.

options.label: Everything always showing
options.desc: The whole unfolded panel from your screenshot, every time. It's taller, so the meals start lower.

items.title: Exercise Drawings to Match the Muscle Maps
items.why:
Honest status: 34 of Goku's 183 exercises use real drawings (Everkinetic, free license, like Push-up below). The other 149 use Goku's own stick figures, which are drawn by code from joint angles. Code-drawn shapes can be improved but won't reach the muscle maps' hand-drawn detail. Option B shows the best I could do that way.

Real drawings for the rest have to come from sets that are free to use. I haven't yet checked how many more Everkinetic or other free sets cover, so the count for A is unknown until I look. No copied images.

now.caption: Now: one of the 34 real drawings

options.label: Find more real drawings; hide stick figures where none exist
options.desc: I search free-license sets and match each one by eye, like the first 34. Exercises still without one show the muscle map and steps only (picture C).

options.label: Code-drawn body shapes in the muscle map's colors
options.desc: Filled, outlined body parts with the worked part in red. It's a step up from sticks, not parity.

options.label: Just hide the stick figures
options.desc: Muscle map and steps only, for the 149 without a real drawing.

items.title: Similar Problems Found Elsewhere
items.why:
These are the same kinds of problems as your 8, all checked in the code or your screenshots:

1. Serving sizes copied from USDA in capitals: “1 TEASPOON (4.0 g)” would become “1 teaspoon (4 g)”.
2. The calorie split can add up to 101% (“24% · 24% · 53%”). It would be rounded to total 100%.
3. Last Session shows a lone “—” over “reps per minute” before your first workout. It would say “No sessions yet”.
4. “20-min cap” breaks across two lines as “20-” and “min cap” on Home. It would stay together.
5. Sheets have uneven side margins (14 px left, 18 px right) that were only there to make room for the shadows. They'd become 16 and 16.
6. Fold headers like “How you feel today” and “Customize this theme” get the same tap signal as item 8.

options.label: Fix some (say which in the note)

items.title: What This Audit Might Have Wrong
items.why:
• The bottom-bar gap was worked out from the code and a browser, not measured on your iPhone. I'd check it on the iPhone 18 Pro simulator before shipping.
• Title Case would touch hundreds of labels. A few may end up wrong (for example “Log a Rest Day” vs “Log a rest day” mid-sentence). I'd list every changed label in the release notes.
• Ki and gravity: plain levels change words only. Your saved sessions, ghosts and records keep working, because ×10, ×20, ×50 and ×100 map one-to-one to Easy, Medium, Hard and Max.
• Dropped from this list: a “tap hint” tour. It adds a screen, and the tap signals in item 8 should make it unnecessary.
• Not checked: dark mode and the Encore and Plain looks with these changes. I'd screenshot all of them before shipping.
